reasons.plausibility: The hypothesis is scientifically sound, leveraging well-known mechanisms of grain boundary segregation and protective oxide glaze formation in high-temperature wear of alloys, though the specific behavior of the complex FeNiCrCoCu system introduces some uncertainty.
reasons.testability: The proposed test is clear and feasible, with a well-defined falsification criterion based on quantitative wear and microstructural analysis, though the practical challenge of decoupling segregation effects from other annealing-induced changes is not fully addressed.
reasons.usefulness: The hypothesis is highly useful as it proposes a specific, controllable microstructural engineering strategy (post-deposition annealing) to directly address the governing mechanism of high-temperature wear resistance in this coating system.
